audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill / Jayce / Jayce / Skill / Skill / Jayce / Jayce, but whys[3] through whys[6] all describe Cho'Gath winning — 'now out-trade and out-heal his poke', 'threatens a flat kill', 'too thick for his burst', 'unlike a true scaler he never reclaims this'. Cho'Gath's win rate here is 58.22% over 493 games, the highest in the slice, and the packet chart gives him levels 4-5 onward. I did NOT change it.
audit.why: The already-audited mirror audits/top/jayce__chogath.json carries the identical chart and explicitly marked point 2 'correct', yet its own rewritten mid says 'this is where it slips away from you' and its late says 'you lose this outright'. Both sides therefore have the same internal contradiction, and flipping only my side would make the two pages disagree and get overwritten by mirror-fix.js. This needs deciding once for both directions, so I left the chart alone and raised it as a question.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phase whys were generic template text; the level-6 line said only 'Jayce's ultimate changes the math too', which is actively misleading because his R is not a power spike ultimate.
audit.why: Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer is a flat 6-second stance swap available from level 1, not a level-6 spike — so the only thing that changes at 6 is Feast (80/70/60s, 175 range, true damage against a champion who builds almost no MR). Thundering Blow is 20/18/16/14/12/10s and is the real trading clock; Q is 16/14/12/10/8/6s.
audit.corrected: Level 6 now says Feast is 175-range true damage against his low MR and that his R is only a 6s stance swap; the trading phases key off Thundering Blow's 20s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Interaction fields said only 'His main poke. Dodge it.' and tracked Shock Blast as the cooldown to bait. Separately, mid and wants.you[0] assert that Feral Scream's silence 'locks his stance-swap' — an unverified claim that the mirror audit records as unverified in the opposite direction.
audit.why: Thundering Blow (E, 20s at rank 1, 240 range) knocks Cho'Gath back and is the ability that takes him out of his own Rupture-into-Feral Scream window — that is the cooldown worth counting, not Shock Blast, which shares the 16s Q timer and is a dodgeable skillshot. Riot's text gives no answer on whether a silence blocks the weapon swap, and the two pages currently claim opposite things, so I removed the assertion from my side rather than restate it.
audit.corrected: Thundering Blow knocks you out of Rupture range — bait its 20s, then knock up and silence.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and content.late are written in the first person — 'This is where I take over', 'I keep snowballing all game here'.
audit.why: The rest of the page addresses the player in second person; the mirror audit made the same conversion on its side.
audit.corrected: mid and late converted to second person inside the length band.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Identify how Jayce contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: You both have weak level 1s — he starts hammer Q to poke last-hits with no all-in yet. Contest CS at max range and set the wave.

edits.before: W silence starts flipping his combo windows. Only take the trade when Jayce's Shock Blast is down.
edits.after: Shock Blast through the Acceleration Gate out-pokes you before Carnivore stabilises — concede CS.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Jayce must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Another point of poke chunks you and one combo cannot out-heal it yet — farm safe and wait for your level 4-6 spike.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Shock Blast's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Carnivore and the Rupture-into-Feral Scream chain out-heal his poke — engage once Thundering Blow (20s at rank 1) is down.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Jayce's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast (80s) is 175-range true damage that ignores his low MR, so any step into Rupture range risks a flat kill. His R is only a 6s stance swap.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Shock Blast's cooldown.
edits.after: Heartsteel plus a Feast stack makes you too thick for his burst — force short trades.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Jayce carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He stays a ranged poke threat near objectives, but stacked HP and true-damage Feast own the 1v1. Carry threat 8/10.

edits.before: Track Jayce's Shock Blast: His main poke. Dodge it. When it is down — Q-W + R him.
edits.after: Thundering Blow knocks you out of Rupture range — bait its 20s, then knock up and silence.

edits.before: - Jayce Shock Blast: matchup-defining — His main poke. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Jayce Thundering Blow: matchup-defining — 20s at rank 1, and it is what knocks you out of your own combo. Shock Blast shares Q's 16s at rank 1; his R is only a 6s swap. - Feast: kill windows only.

edits.before: Q under Jayce's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Rupture under Jayce's feet as he steps up, Feral Scream to cut the poke, then E-spike — commit only once Thundering Blow is spent.

edits.before: This is where I take over. By levels 4-5 my Carnivore sustain plus Vorpal Spikes heal his poke faster than he can land it, and my Rupture-into-Feral-Scream combo punishes any step-up — the knockup sets up the cone, and the up-to-2-second silence locks his stance-swap so he can't burst back. At 6, Feast is a true-damage execute that blows through his low MR, so every time he walks up to poke he's risking a flat kill. Wait out his Thundering Blow knockback, then Q-W him when it's on cooldown.
edits.after: This is where you take over. By levels 4-5 Carnivore sustain plus Vorpal Spikes heal his poke faster than he can land it, and your Rupture-into-Feral-Scream combo punishes any step-up — the knockup sets up the cone and the silence denies his cannon-Q and his Thundering Blow. At 6, Feast is a true-damage execute that blows through his low MR, so every time he walks up to poke he risks a flat kill. Wait out Thundering Blow (20s at rank 1), then Q-W him while it is down.

edits.before: I keep snowballing all game here — this isn't a scaler matchup that reclaims late like Vayne or Fiora. Once my HP and tank components stack with Feast, his cannon-poke and hammer burst simply can't chunk me anymore, and my Rupture-Feral-Scream lockdown plus true-damage Feast let me delete him or peel him off my carries in every fight. He stays a ranged poke threat, so close walls and don't facecheck a charged cannon-Q, but the 1v1 and the teamfight are both mine.

edits.before: Land Rupture to knock him up, then chain Feral Scream so the silence stops his stance-swap and denies the cannon-Q poke and Thundering Blow knockback

notes: CHART LEFT UNCHANGED ON PURPOSE — see the point-2 audit entry and questionsForUser. My chart and the already-audited jayce__chogath chart are identical (Skill/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Skill/Jayce/Jayce), so the mirror is consistent, but BOTH pages' prose says Cho'Gath takes over from level 4 and never gives it back, and the win rate is 58.22%. Flipping one side alone would just be reverted by mirror-fix.js, so this needs one decision applied to both. Also removed, not restated: the claim that Feral Scream's silence locks Jayce's stance swap. The mirror audit records the opposite claim as unverified; Riot's text is silent and needsResearch is empty, so neither page should assert it. Cho'Gath's kit flags Rupture as 'grounding'; Riot's description says it pops enemies into the air, so I wrote knockup.
